Hi Elena — great questions and very reasonable for accelerator flows. TL;DR: yes to nonlinear scheduling and yes to rule-based top-ups; we have a couple of implementation patterns depending on accounting needs.

High level options:
- Tapered allocation: issue chunked credits at defined milestones (sign, mid-cohort, graduation). Credits consume against hosted usage and are visible in the Console per-company.
- Triggered top-ups: create a webhook/metric hook to release an auto-credit when a threshold is met (e.g., 1M API calls or $X ARR). We can tie releases to your cohort tracker or HubSpot deal stages.
- Invoice split: we can route billing charges to multiple payer entities and tag credits against specific sponsors; operationally the sponsor-split appears as separate invoice lines.

I'll attach a short draft proposal with two concrete schedules and a sample clause for sponsor invoicing. Vanessa, Ben — can you confirm the standard policy for sponsor-split invoices and whether legal needs specific language for auto-release (DocuSign + SLA)?

Sending draft now.

— Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Elena — quick note from finance/ops side: we can do sponsor-split invoicing but need the following to avoid reconciliation friction:

- A sponsor allocation table at t=sign (simple CSV mapping company -> sponsor share)
- Clear event definitions for "triggered top-up" (metric name, threshold, measurement window) so ledger entries are deterministic
- If sponsors want credits tagged to specific sponsor IDs, we can attach metadata for audit and reporting.

Ben — is there a guardrail on auto-credit frequency? We usually limit auto-release to once per 30 days per company unless there is an explicit conversion to committed (reserved) capacity.

Elena — if that's acceptable I'll include a short ops checklist in the draft and a sample invoice split template.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Looping in a pricing guardrail: Jordan and Vanessa captured the operational pieces. From a discount/commit perspective I recommend the following package for accelerators to keep conversion funnels simple:

- Initial welcome pool: 15,000 credits per startup at sign
- Mid-cohort top-up: 5,000 credits unlocked at demo day subject to active engagement (>=3 product calls)
- Graduation top-up: 5,000 credits on graduation if cohort company opens a conversion discussion within 90 days
- Triggered top-up: one additional 10,000 credits per company, auto-released when they hit the agreed usage threshold (we limit to one auto-release per company pre-conversion).

For sponsor invoicing: we'll invoice sponsors monthly with separate line items and include a reconciliation appendix. If legal needs to limit auto-credit liability, propose a cap (e.g., total credits released via top-ups <= 50k/company) — open to negotiation.

Happy to set this as an offer in HubSpot and hand to your legal for a simple SOW-addendum.

— Ben Carter
Head of Startup Programs, Redwood Inference
